Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below; I attached a data map and an erase runbook for your security team to review.

1) Region pinning: Redwood Dedicated supports tenant-level region affinity. For SummitTech we will pin the tenant to the US-West region at provisioning. Automatic cross-region failover is disabled for your tenancy by default; we only enable cross-region routing under a predefined emergency policy and only with written customer approval. We will include a clause in the SOW that specifies the pinned region and the conditions under which we could re-route requests.

2) Deletion/erase process: attached is our Erase_Runbook_v1.2.docx. Summary: upon termination request we initiate a coordinated pipeline that includes (a) snapshot freeze, (b) KV cache flush, (c) live workload drain, (d) deletion of tenant-specific object storage buckets, (e) scrubbing of control-plane metadata, (f) cryptographic key rotation and tombstoning of snapshots, and (g) verification sweep. Typical timeline: 7–14 calendar days from approved termination request for logical deletion; 30–45 days for physical media sanitization depending on cloud provider processes. For Dedicated customers requiring faster RPOs we can negotiate a compressed timeline in the contract.

I also attached a Dedicated_Data_Map.pdf with the services and data flows. Ben has the technical checklist; looping him in for any infra specifics.

Next steps: if procurement/legal wants an explicit SOW paragraph and acceptance criteria for deletion, our contracts team can draft.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick technical addendum from infra:
- The Dedicated deployment for SummitTech will be provisioned into a tenant-scoped VPC in the us-west-2 (Oregon) subnet set; all compute, cache, and storage are logically isolated to that region.
- Backups: daily snapshots are stored in-region by default. If SummitTech requests cross-region replication we will only enable it under an explicit written change control request.
- Evidence: we can provide a post-provisioning verification package (network ACL screenshots, IAM role manifests, and snapshot metadata) and an audit log bundle for the deletion event.
- Sanity check on timelines: the 7–14 day logical wipe is dependent on queued jobs and mounted snapshots; the 30–45 day physical retention is provider-bound. For customers requiring cryptographic destruction evidences (HSM/KMS logs), we can include that in the package.

If you want, I can prepare a terse one-page technical affidavit for your security team.

—Ben
